message.content:
Ableton’s stock devices can absolutely cover evolving, hypnotic textures and tuned resonant percussion—but for many of the specific combinations you’re asking about there are **no good, focused tutorials** yet, especially for Live 12–specific workflows (Roar modulation for hypnotic textures, Echo’s modulation tab in depth, DS FM/Clang/Tom, Auto Filter Spin). Below I’ll stick strictly to what is actually documented or in named tutorials, and say explicitly when there isn’t a source.

Because I cannot browse further right now, I can only cite the URLs that appeared in the previous tool call; anything not backed by one of those URLs I’ll flag as *not sourced*.

---

## 1. Corpus & Resonators – tuned resonant percussion in key

### a) Tuning Corpus to the key / to other tracks

A dedicated tutorial on tuning and MIDI pitch tracking in Corpus is “Ableton Live Tutorials: Introduction to the Corpus Device” and several deep‑dives:

- Introduction to Corpus (audio + MIDI routing, LFO, stereo image):  
  https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=fkWktUOqGMA  
- General tutorial on Corpus as resonator:  
  https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=MBZjzHTNe2o  
- Deep dive, including tuning and pitch tracking:  
  https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=LWJ6HCkXu3w  

From these:

- **Corpus is a resonator that layers a modeled physical resonant body over the input signal.**[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=MBZjzHTNe2o]  
- In the deep dive, the presenter demonstrates **tuning via the Frequency (Hz) / MIDI note values, and using Dry/Wet at 50% to blend the resonator percussion with the source**.[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=LWJ6HCkXu3w]

Concrete, sourced technique:

1. **Pitch‑tracking via MIDI sidechain**  
   The intro tutorial walks through routing MIDI into Corpus to control pitch over time.[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=fkWktUOqGMA]  
   - Put **Corpus** on an audio track (e.g. hi‑hat loop).  
   - Create a MIDI track with a clip containing the notes of your track’s scale.  
   - Route that MIDI track’s output to the Corpus track’s MIDI sidechain input (shown in the tutorial).[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=fkWktUOqGMA]  
   - Enable “frequency via MIDI” in Corpus so that **Corpus’ pitch follows the notes played by that external MIDI instrument**.[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=JiQm0kzN1xY]  

   In the “Corpus” tutorial at 4:25+, the author explicitly shows **Corpus listening to a bass line, so the percussion resonances are pitched to the bass notes**, i.e. in key.[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=JiQm0kzN1xY]

2. **Tuning manually**  
   In the deep dive, the presenter sets **Dry/Wet to 100%** to hear only the resonator, then uses the tuning section (Frequency / Note) to lock to pitch.[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=LWJ6HCkXu3w]  
   Concrete numbers are not explicitly given in the video transcript; the workflow is to use the **note‑based tuning control** to match the key and then fine‑tune by ear.[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=LWJ6HCkXu3w]  
   Because no numeric values (e.g. “set Frequency to 440 Hz”) are stated in the sources, I cannot give sourced numbers for tuning beyond this.

3. **Using factory presets for tuned percussion**  
   In an Ableton user group post, someone recommends dropping the **“Punchy Snare” Corpus preset** onto a snare to add resonant crunch.[https://www.facebook.com/groups/abletonliveusers/posts/9313471412096406/]  
   That’s a concrete “start here” for tuned snare/resonant percussion; however, exact parameter values (e.g. specific Hz) are not enumerated in the post.

Unsourced (I must flag this):  
- Any statement like “set Corpus Frequency to 55 Hz for A1” or “Resonators set to mix 40%, decay 3 s” is not in the sources I have; those values would be typical practice, but not backed by a URL, so I will not present them as sourced technique.

### b) Resonators device, tuned to key

I do not have a direct Resonators‑specific tutorial URL in the retrieved results.  
The Ableton manual page that was retrieved is for **Audio Effect Reference**, not specifically Resonators, but shows a similar idea for **Spectral Resonator**: using MIDI to create tonal drum loops.[https://www.ableton.com/en/manual/live-audio-effect-reference/]

So:

- **There is no good, specific tutorial URL in the retrieved sources for tuning Resonators to the key of a track.**  
- Ableton’s manual (Audio Effect Reference) would describe the Resonators device’s **Note / Frequency** parameter, but I do not have a snippet clearly describing numeric values or a “tuned percussion” walkthrough.[https://www.ableton.com/en/manual/live-audio-effect-reference/]

## 3. Spectral Resonator (Modes, Mod Rate, Pch Mod)

The Ableton Live **Audio Effect Reference** mentions Spectral Resonator and tonal drum loops:

- The manual explicitly states: “Create tonal drum loops by placing Spectral Resonator on a drum track and using the MIDI sidechain input to drive specific pitches.”[https://www.ableton.com/en/manual/live-audio-effect-reference/]

Concrete, sourced workflow:

1. **Tonal drum loops via MIDI sidechain**  
   - Put **Spectral Resonator** on a drum audio track.[https://www.ableton.com/en/manual/live-audio-effect-reference/]  
   - Use the device’s MIDI sidechain input to receive notes from a MIDI track; this drives which **pitches** are being resonated.[https://www.ableton.com/en/manual/live-audio-effect-reference/]  
   - This yields tuned resonances in the key of the MIDI pattern.

The manual, however, does not give numeric values for **Modes, Mod Rate, Pch Mod** in the snippet I have, nor a “hypnotic texture” recipe. So:

- **There is no sourced tutorial in the retrieved results that walks through specific Mod Rate / Pitch Mod values for evolving hypnotic textures with Spectral Resonator.**

---

## 4. Granulator III – evolving textures

Ableton’s official blog “Explore Micro-Sound Design in Granulator III with dnksaus” gives a high‑level workflow:

- The article describes **crafting ethereal vocal slices, “otherworldly botanical textures,” and glitchy scrub patterns** using controls like **Position, Key, Glide, I/O, and the built‑in LFO.**[https://www.ableton.com/en/blog/sound-design-with-granulator-iii/]  

This is a named, official tutorial:

- **Explore Micro-Sound Design in Granulator III with dnksaus**  
  https://www.ableton.com/en/blog/sound-design-with-granulator-iii/

Concrete, sourced aspects:

- Use any sample as the source; the article mentions **ethereal vocal slices** and **botanical textures** as examples.[https://www.ableton.com/en/blog/sound-design-with-granulator-iii/]  
- The workflow leans on **Position modulation and the built‑in LFO** to create movement.[https://www.ableton.com/en/blog/sound-design-with-granulator-iii/]  

The YouTube video “Texture galore with Granulator III in Live 12” demonstrates use of the device as a texture synthesizer:

- The author explains Granulator III as a **granular synthesizer using a sample instead of an oscillator** and shows dropping arbitrary samples then building textures.[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=GR6ToaUcLQo]

However:

- Neither the blog nor the YouTube snippet I have contains explicit numeric values like “set grain size to 80 ms, jitter to 0.3” in the text I can see, so I cannot supply sourced numeric parameters.

## 5. Roar – modulation matrix for evolving saturation / textures

There are multiple named tutorials on **Roar** and its modulation matrix:

### a) “The ultimate guide to Roar…” (MusicRadar)

- “The ultimate guide to Roar, the gnarly saturation plugin that's the …” is a detailed written tutorial.[https://www.musicradar.com/news/ultimate-guide-to-ableton-live-12-roar]  

Concrete, sourced parameters:

- The article says: **“We’re going to use LFO 1 to modulate, so set its speed value to a relatively low 1 as shown in red.”** This is a specific numeric setting (LFO 1 speed = 1).[https://www.musicradar.com/news/ultimate-guide-to-ableton-live-12-roar]  
- Then: **“Now click and drag up in the newly-created Drive cell under LFO 1 to 30 and you will hear Roar pulse with each LFO cycle.”** So Drive modulation amount = 30.[https://www.musicradar.com/news/ultimate-guide-to-ableton-live-12-roar]

That’s a concrete hypnotic‑style pulsation of saturation:

- Put Roar on a bass or texture;  
- Set **LFO 1 speed to 1** (project‑synced; article indicates a slow pulsing).[https://www.musicradar.com/news/ultimate-guide-to-ableton-live-12-roar]  
- Map **LFO 1 → Drive** in the modulation matrix, set amount to **30** to hear pulsing saturation.[https://www.musicradar.com/news/ultimate-guide-to-ableton-live-12-roar]  

The same article also uses **Envelope modulation up to 100** in the matrix to explore envelope‑driven saturation changes (Drive/Tone).[https://www.musicradar.com/news/ultimate-guide-to-ableton-live-12-roar]

### b) YouTube tutorials: modulation matrix

Several Live 12 Roar videos show modulation matrix use:

- “5 Ways to Use ROAR in Ableton Live 12”  
  https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=q8XnRLlOyA4  
  The presenter shows mapping LFOs and the envelope follower to Roar filter frequency and other parameters via the modulation matrix, explicitly pointing out the **LFO 1 / LFO 2 / Envelope / Noise** sources.[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=q8XnRLlOyA4]

- “New in Ableton Live 12: Roar – Extremely Versatile Audio Effect for Colouration and Saturation”  
  https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=t9I_gvLTte0  
  This video describes Roar’s **feedback routing, large modulation matrix, and separate compressor section**, and indicates mapping parameters via the matrix for complex modulation.[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=t9I_gvLTte0]

- “All About ROAR In Ableton Live & And How To Apply It (Bass & Drums)”  
  https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=8QZE2-zv8-0  
  Shows the modulation matrix with **LFO1, LFO2, envelope follower and noise** as sources and mapping them to various destinations.[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=8QZE2-zv8-0]

- “Ableton Roar Explained – The Only Guide You’ll Ever Need”  
  https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=4_U7Jdk-K7g  
  States Roar is “a saturation coloration device with up to three processing stages, different saturation types, feedback, compression, and a bunch of modulation options.”[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=4_U7Jdk-K7g]  
  The presenter shows mapping **LFO 1 to Blend at 100%** in the modulation matrix.[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=4_U7Jdk-K7g]

Concrete, sourced parameter:

- In that video, **LFO 1 → Blend amount set to 100%** is explicitly mentioned: “We need to click on blend. And we are going to assign LFO one to blend 100%.”[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=4_U7Jdk-K7g]

So for evolving hypnotic saturation textures:

- Use **Roar** on a pad or percussion bus.  
- In the Mod Matrix, assign **LFO 1 → Blend, amount 100%**, as per the tutorial, to morph between processing stages over time.[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=4_U7Jdk-K7g]  
- Combine with **LFO 1 speed = 1, Drive amount = 30** from the MusicRadar guide for slow pulsing distortion.[https://www.musicradar.com/news/ultimate-guide-to-ableton-live-12-roar]

This is all sourced.

## 9. Grain Delay – evolving hypnotic textures

There is a named tutorial with explicit, concrete guidance:

- “Craft Lush Evolving Textures with Ease with Ableton Live’s Grain Delay”  
  https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=PtFsOllynYs  

This video gives clear procedural instructions with parameter mentions:

- Start by dropping Grain Delay onto a **sustained sound like a pad or vocal note.**[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=PtFsOllynYs]  
- Use the **Spray** parameter: “Spray scatters grains randomly across time; higher spray values combined with low frequency settings create spacious textures.”[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=PtFsOllynYs]  
- Automate the **Pitch** parameter to add gentle harmonic shifts and evolution.[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=PtFsOllynYs]  
- Increase **Feedback** gradually to build density, but avoid too‑high values to prevent overwhelming the mix.[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=PtFsOllynYs]  
- Use **Random Pitch** for subtle detuning and movement.[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=PtFsOllynYs]  
- The tutorial suggests **layering multiple Grain Delay instances**, one set with high Spray for diffuse textures, another with synced delay times for rhythmic elements.[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=PtFsOllynYs]  
- It also recommends combining Grain Delay with **chorus or phaser** for extra movement, and using **Dry/Wet to blend** effect with the original audio.[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=PtFsOllynYs]

Note: the transcript snippet does not show numeric values (e.g. “Spray = 0.5”); the guidance is descriptive (“higher spray values,” “low frequency settings”) but not numerically precise. So:

- **We have a good tutorial with qualitative parameter guidance but no explicit numeric parameter values in the text snippet.**
